newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: TWO TO FACE COURT OVER EXPLOSION CHARGES
Two-men will face court this morning over yesterday's explosion in Sydney that destroyed a home.
Police believe petrol was used in the blast at Woollahra...nearby buildings were also damaged, including the Turkish consulate.
Detectives don't believe there's any link between the attack and the consulate.
The men, aged 25 and 29, were interviewed and charged over the blast after being treated in hospital for burns.
The pair is due to face Waverley Court later this morning.
POLICE PLAYING EXTORTIONIST WAITING GAME
Police in Queensland and New South Wales will be waiting for the Arnott's biscuits extortionist to make the next move today.
The extortionist had threatened to release poisoned Arnott's biscuits in the two states today, but the company has removed all its biscuits from shops.
The extortionist wants New South Wales police to take a public lie detector test over evidence in the trial of Ronald Henry Thomas, who was found guilty of a double murder on the Gold Coast in 1991.
Police want to speak to John Victor Bobak, Thomas' co-accused, who's been on the run since the murders.
Police say there's no immediate threat to consumers from the extortionist, but are waiting to see if any new threats or demands are made.
DOCTOR: PATIENTS MAY SAY THINGS THEY DON'T MEAN
A prominent Victorian cancer specialist has urged doctors not to automatically take at face value patients saying they wish they were dead.
In an article on voluntary euthanasia in the Australian Medical Journal, Dr John Zalcberg claims people expressing such sentiments often don't mean what they say.
He says the danger of the Northern Territory voluntary euthanasia law is that doctors may be more inclined to accept that patients wanting to access it don't want to continue living.
PERTH FIREFIGHTERS BATTLE TO CONTAIN BLAZE
Firefighters in Perth's Hills region are still working to bring a bushfire under control, more that 24 hours after it first broke out.
A Bush Fires Board spokesman says much of the blaze has been contained, but it's still burning out of control on its eastern flank near Gilchrist Road in Lesmurdie.
He says firefighters have managed to save several homes which were threatened, but more than 500 hectares of bushland has been burnt out.
The spokesman says teams will remain in the region overnight to ensure there are no fresh outbreaks.
